obtained.how: University of Wisconsin Digital Collections scan (institutional library copy, open access), with text layer

bibliography.note: Kleinert, Stanton J. & Mraz, Donald. 1966. Life history of the grass pickerel (Esox americanus vermiculatus) in southeastern Wisconsin. Wisconsin Conservation Department Technical Bulletin Number 37, Madison. As cited.

claims.quote: The lake covers 138 acres with a maximum depth of 32 feet
claims.conditions: landlocked kettle lake, Walworth County; average depth 15 ft

claims.claim: Fall Schnabel estimates 1962–65: grass pickerel 22–97/ha (1.2–3.9 kg/ha) over four autumns
claims.conditions: fall electrofishing mark–recapture, Schnabel method; 5,419, 3,121, 1,300 and 1,240 fish (39.3, 22.6, 9.4, 9.0 per acre); 483.0, 276.0, 151.8, 193.2 lb (3.5, 2.0, 1.1, 1.4 lb/acre)
claims.note: 39.3 × 2.471 = 97.1/ha; 9.0 × 2.471 = 22.2/ha; 3.5 lb/acre × 1.121 = 3.9 kg/ha; 1.1 × 1.121 = 1.2 kg/ha. The authors say the shocker could not work in water < 2 ft or dense weeds and under-sampled fingerlings, so 1964–65 are underestimates and the direction of the 1962–63 error is unknown (pp. 14–16).

claims.claim: The decline was driven by year-class failure when drought stranded the nursery
claims.quote: declining water levels in 1964 and 1965, stranding many fingerlings and adults
claims.conditions: 'partial failure of the 1964 and 1965 year classes'; local precipitation 'well below normal' fall 1962–fall 1965, lake level fell 24 inches; the slough was cut off from the lake by early July 1964 and 1965 and dried

claims.claim: When falling water cut off a slough nursery, grass pickerel year classes were three to four times smaller
claims.source_value: Young-of-year counts in the fall electrofishing catch were 178 (1962), 205 (1963), 42 (1964) and 78 (1965): 1964 was 4.2–4.9 times smaller than 1962–63 and 1965 2.3–2.6 times smaller. These are catches of fish under 7 in by a shocker that under-sampled fingerlings, not year-class estimates; the authors call it a 'partial failure'.
claims.conditions: fall shocker surveys of 38, 24, 22.5 and 20 h (Table 4); the 1964 figure equals the Table 2 count of pickerel < 7 in
claims.note: Say 'about 2.5 to 5 times fewer young-of-year in the fall catch' or give the four numbers.

claims.claim: 95.8 % of grass pickerel under 7 in (178 mm) in a Wisconsin lake came from one 6-ha vegetated bay and slough
claims.source_value: 95.8 % is the 1963 share of shocker-caught pickerel under 7 in that came from the East Bay; it was 66.7 % in 1964 and 51.3 % in 1965 as the bay shrank. The slough could not be shocked; East Bay and slough together are 15 acres (6.1 ha).
claims.quote: 95.8, 66.7, and 51.3 percent came from the East Bay in 1963, 1964 and 1965
claims.conditions: fall electrofishing; 1962 'almost all' pickerel 4–7 in came from the East Bay; the bay and slough are 'the main spawning and nursery areas'
claims.note: Give the year (1963, high water) and the bay (not bay and slough), or the 1963–65 range 51–96 %.

claims.claim: Young grass pickerel at Pleasant Lake grew ~0.85–0.9 mm/d from late May to mid-September (project calculation)
claims.source_value: Inputs: last-week-of-May means 33.0, 33.5 and 28.0 mm (1963–65) and mid-September means 132.5 (1963), 122.5 (1964) and late-September 126.0 mm (1965). Assuming 28 May → 15 September (110 d) and 25 September for 1965 (120 d): 0.90, 0.81 and 0.82 mm/d (mean 0.84), i.e. about 0.8–0.9 mm/d.
claims.quote: Length averages for fingerlings caught the last week of May were 33.0 mm. in 1963
claims.conditions: May fish seined in the slough; September fish caught by the fall shocker in the East Bay (which missed small fingerlings, so the autumn means may run high); lengths in mm (total length, per the paper's figures)
claims.note: Minor: two of the three years fall just below 0.85; '~0.8–0.9 mm/d' fits all three.

claims.claim: In grass pickerel, 2 % of 351 young-of-year had eaten pickerel and no adult had
claims.quote: only 7 of 351 grass pickerel less than 112.0 mm. having eaten other pickerel
claims.conditions: 351 fingerling stomachs from the Pleasant Lake nursery, 1963–65; 7/351 = 2.0 %; adults: a combined sample of 267 pickerel 6.0–13.5 in from four lakes, 104 with food
claims.note: Second half: 'None of the stomachs of adult pickerel examined in the present study contained other pickerel.' One 37-mm fingerling held 13 pickerel of 6.5–11.5 mm.

claims.claim: Grass pickerel in a 6-ha Michigan lake (rotenone): ~50 young-of-year/ha (project arithmetic; Carbine & Applegate 1948 via Kleinert & Mraz 1966)
claims.quote: 369 grass pickerel following rotenone poisoning in a 14.8-acre Michigan lake
claims.conditions: '(24.9 per acre) — 81.2 percent of these were young-of-the-year'; no date or season given here
claims.note: 369 × 0.812 = 300 young-of-year; 14.8 acres = 5.99 ha; 300/5.99 = 50/ha. The table is headed 'late summer and autumn', but Kleinert & Mraz give no date for the census.

notes: Other values useful to the rewrite: spawning in the East Bay slough right after ice-out at 40–53 °F, lasting about two weeks (pp. 18–19); yearling males and females mature (p. 19); fecundity 625–4,584 mature eggs at 6.3–12.8 in (Table 5); hatch in 11–15 days at 46–48 °F (p. 22); fingerling diet by length (pp. 28–29: cladocerans and copepods to 15 mm; chironomids, Odonata and fish from 15–40 mm; zooplankton rare above 40 mm); adult stomachs 93 of 104 with fish, mainly small bluegill and pumpkinseed (p. 31); a spring spawning-run estimate of 1,274 fish in 1963 (p. 19).
